source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #267 (branch fix/200-aot-load-split at head f988123a67220089cba96f5e8b960c15498ddcb5 — branch commit f3746033c8bec2629df9865cf6f71dd1f235d85b with current main 2505d8c merged in at merge commit d5acd0b43042e7d655199f2690f5090f27273ecc, plus two merge follow-up fixes, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45120276581 and 45120284790 against the branch and pull-request run 45120209665, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #267 (#200, split the AoT load path from the JIT emitters). The PR adds a non-default ‘aot-load’ feature to the telomere crate (store code cache, runtime stubs, native-call ABI and executable code memory, but no compiler) and makes ‘jit’ imply it plus the codegen crate’s new ‘emit’ feature for the assembler/emitter layer; in an aot-load-only build a compile request consults the cache only and otherwise reports the typed VMResult::Unimplemented so the interpreter takes over. It also adds the core-aot configuration to the footprint ladder and to this gate, and a symbol checker (tools/check-aot-load-symbols.py) asserting emitter symbols are absent from an aot-load-only embedder. Landing it required merging current main (PR #265, #197’s EmitEnv generalisation, and PR #266, #209’s trap-site tables) into the branch: the module declarations in runtime/jit.rs conflicted and were resolved on the PR’s classification (stubs and profile are load side, aot-load; emit_env and the reloc tests are emitter side, jit), and two follow-up fixes were needed — #209’s resolve_trap_site, whose only caller is the aot-load entry bridge, is gated aot-load instead of jit (body unchanged), and the PR’s corpus measurement harness reads EmittedFunction.code now that #209 returns the code plus the trap-site table. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (2505d8c) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45120292330, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 14 gated series main measures (main has no core-aot configuration), so every delta is this PR’s own. The deltas are confined to the two configurations that link the native-code machinery and are pure code-layout shift from the cfg refactor: core-jit (release stripped file +336 B / stripped .text +304 B; release-size stripped file +32 B / stripped .text +16 B) and core-aot (release stripped file +88 B / stripped .text +80 B; release-size stripped file +56 B / stripped .text +80 B, against the first values this PR recorded for the new series from a fleur measurement; the CI-measured values recorded here supersede those). The other 12 of the 16 gated series are byte-identical. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (16 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
